item.title: The Signal: The Parties Are Choosing Sides. Will the Voters Follow?
item.description: Tinubu’s political alliances are expanding, Obi and Kwankwaso are sharpening their challenge, and INEC is under pressure to demonstrate transparency. But as the presidential campaign gathers momentum, Nigeria’s politicians may be discovering that winning endorsements is easier than winning public confidence. There is an interesting contradiction emerging in Nigerian politics. At a time when political parties are supposed to be competing against one another, their leading figures are increasingly finding reasons to work together. In Rivers State, Nyesom Wike is assembling a coalition that crosses party boundaries but supports President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. In Osun, Governor Ademola Adeleke supports Tinubu’s re-election while insisting that his political organisation will compete against the APC in legislative elections. Meanwhile, Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have established a joint presidential campaign structure, even as other opposition leaders continue discussing the possibility of a broader alliance. And the Independent National Electoral Commission, caught in the middle of growing political suspicion, has taken a step towards addressing concerns about the voters’ register. Welcome to Nigeria’s 2027 election. A contest in which party labels are becoming increasingly flexible, political loyalties are being renegotiated, and the electorate is being asked to distinguish between genuine conviction and political convenience. But beneath the manoeuvring lies a question that could determine the outcome. The politicians are choosing sides. Will the voters follow them? Wike’s coalition: when political boundaries become optional Nyesom Wike has never been a politician easily constrained by conventional party loyalties. His support for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, despite his association with the PDP, demonstrated his willingness to pursue political objectives across party lines. Now, with another presidential election approaching, he is taking that approach further. At a political gathering in Eleme, Rivers State, Wike made it clear that his Rainbow Coalition is not simply an arrangement to support Tinubu’s re-election. It also intends to support APC candidates contesting governorship and legislative elections. That is a significant development. It suggests that Wike is attempting to create a political structure capable of influencing elections at several levels, regardless of the formal party affiliations of those participating. There is a certain political logic to the arrangement. For Tinubu, Wike provides an influential ally in a strategically important state. For Wike, cooperation with the President offers a means of preserving political relevance and strengthening his position in Rivers. But what does the arrangement offer ordinary voters? item.title: Trump says Putin-Zelensky meeting to be set up ‘very soon’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky would be set up “very soon.” The announcement came as Trump’s administration ramps up diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year. “There’ll be a meeting set up very soon and I think a lot of progress could be made,” Trump told reporters. Zelensky said on Sunday that a trilateral meeting between Kyiv, Washington and Moscow would take place in November, aiming to restart stalled peace talks. The Kremlin had previously said that a meeting between the three countries was planned to take place in the United Arab Emirates in November. Putin, who ordered the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Zelensky and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine. Trump came to power in January 2025 promising to end the war in 24 hours — but over a year of US-led talks have failed to produce a breakthrough, with tens of thousands killed. In recent days Trump has once again pivoted away from Ukraine and back to Putin, trumpeting what he said was a deal for Russia to sell diesel and reduce prices sent soaring by his Iran war. item.title: FG moves to secure farms, attract investors
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has moved to address insecurity threatening agricultural investments, signing a partnership agreement to develop security arrangements for farms and attract investors to multibillion-dollar soybean and sugarcane projects in Yobe and Jigawa states. The Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI), Integranium Holdings and Defence Agricultural Assets and Projects Development Company (DAPCO), supported by Defence Holding Company Limited, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abuja. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Dr Femi Ogunseinde, MOFI’s Executive Director, Investments, said: “We have a soybean initiative in Yobe, we have a sugarcane initiative in Jigawa—all large-scale, all multibillion-dollar projects. “Without having that security anchor to ensure that whatever comes from wherever to invest, the investments are safe, it becomes very difficult for us to do anything.” He said the partnership would provide a platform to approach prospective investors with security arrangements designed to protect their investments. Also speaking, the Managing Director of MOFI, Dr Armstrong Takang, said: “Nigeria needed to make better use of its land, water resources and people to produce sufficient food for households and industries, while generating additional supplies for export.” He said the partnership would focus on developing bankable agribusiness opportunities capable of attracting public and private investment. On his part, DAPCO Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Aliyu Abdulhameed, said: “The defence establishment’s role was to ensure that financing reached agricultural opportunities in rural areas under secure and properly structured arrangements.” He added that surrounding communities would be involved in projects established in their areas, while serving military personnel and veterans would also be considered. Ogunseinde said: “An estimated 30 million to 35 million hectares of land could be available for farming, providing considerable scope for expanding large-scale agricultural production.” He added that the partners had identified several opportunities and expected at least one project to break ground before year-end, although he did not identify the project or specify a commencement date. The Group Managing Director of Defence Holding Company Limited, Air Vice Marshal A.V. Ndache, said: “The memorandum of understanding signed by the institutions was a broad agreement covering agriculture, hospitality and other investment areas.” The post FG moves to secure farms, attract investors appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FirstBank, GTBank, UBA roll out Google Pay for customers
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe FirstBank, Guaranty Trust Bank (GTBank) and United Bank for Africa (UBA) have rolled out Google Pay for eligible customers, expanding digital payment options following the launch of the global digital wallet service in Nigeria. The integration enables eligible cardholders to add their cards to Google Wallet and make secure digital payments using compatible devices at supported payment terminals and online checkout platforms, locally and internationally. FirstBank Nigeria Limited in a statement said the integration would enable eligible cardholders to make convenient contactless payments while benefiting from Google Pay’s security features and faster checkout experience. Speaking on the development, Abednego Ugwueke, Group Head, e-Business and Retail Products, FirstBank, said: “At FirstBank, we are constantly evolving our digital capabilities to deliver banking experiences that are simple, secure and aligned with the lifestyle of our customers.” He added that the integration would provide eligible cardholders with “a seamless and globally accepted payment solution that enables them to make purchases with confidence wherever Google Pay is accepted.” Similarly, UBA has enabled Google Pay for eligible Visa and Mastercard users, allowing customers to make contactless payments without carrying physical cards. UBA’s Directorate Head, Cards, Orry Seem, said: “Our customers live busy lives, and the way they pay should make those lives easier. For many of them, the phone is the first thing they reach for, so it makes sense for it to become their wallet too.” UBA’s Group Head, Brands, Marketing and Corporate Communications, Alero Ladipo, said: “Digital payment in Nigeria is growing fast, and customers expect more ways to pay. Making Google Pay available to our Visa and Mastercard cardholders gives them a simple, fast option for everyday purchases, backed by the security of their UBA cards.” GTCO, parent company of GTBank, has also integrated Google Pay across two subsidiaries, extending the service to both customers and businesses. GTBank customers can add their debit cards to Google Wallet and use Google Pay for online transactions, including subscriptions, travel bookings, food delivery and bill payments. Through HabariPay’s Squad payment gateway, businesses can also accept Google Pay at checkout. Commenting on the launch, GTCO Group Chief Executive Officer, Segun Agbaje, said the Group was addressing challenges that cause customers to abandon online purchases. “Most failed online payments are not refused, they are abandoned. Somewhere along the way the customer gives up, and the business never learns about the sale it lost,” he said. Agbaje added: “With Google Pay, what matters to us is that we are ready on both sides from the first day: a GTBank customer can pay with it, and a business on Squad can accept it.” HabariPay Managing Director, Eduofon Japhet, said the integration would simplify checkout for merchants. “Squad businesses n

item.title: Cooking gas supply rises 18% to 4.5m litres daily — NMDPRA
item.description: By Ediri Ejoh Domestic supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), popularly known as cooking gas, rose by 17.78 per cent year-on-year, YoY, to 4.5 million litres per day in September 2026, from 3.7 million litres per day in September 2025. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest data obtained by Vanguard. On a month-on-month, MoM, basis, supply increased by 33.33 per cent from 4.5 million litres per day in August 2026. Meanwhile, the price of cooking gas rose by 7.14 per cent to N1,400 per kg in October 2026, from N1,300 per kg in September. Reacting, former National President of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Mr. Oladapo Olatunbosun, attributed the increase to improved local production but called for sustained investment and government support to prevent shortages. He said: “Local production has increased, which is the reason for the result. However, there is much to be done by both the government and stakeholders to drive the development required to harness the potential of LPG.” Olatunbosun urged the government to encourage indigenous operators and support major domestic producers, including Dangote Petroleum Refinery, to boost output and stabilise the energy market. “The government should continue to encourage indigenous operators, and they should see it as being a partner in bringing stability to energy,” he said. He also called for affordable supplies to surrounding communities, adding that increased investment in production and distribution would improve availability. “The market is wide and large, and the more we get people investing in the production and distribution of LPG, the more available the product will be,” he said. Similarly, National President of the Oil and Gas Services Providers Association of Nigeria, OGSPAN, Mazi Colman Obasi, described the supply growth as positive but stressed that consumers must benefit through improved access and affordability. “The growth in supply is a positive development because availability is fundamental to the expansion of LPG consumption. However, the real test is whether consumers are seeing improved access and more affordable prices,” he said. Obasi cautioned that increased supply would not automatically reduce retail prices, citing transportation, logistics, exchange-rate movements and other costs. He said efficient distribution was essential to ensure additional volumes reach consumers and encourage more households to switch to LPG. item.title: 2027: NDC campaign DG urges Atiku to join Obi-Kwankwaso
item.description: The Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkarim, has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other opposition leaders to join the alliance backing Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Abdulkarim said the opposition needed to unite behind a common platform to improve its chances of defeating the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the election. Speaking on Arise News, he said the coalition was already taking shape within the NDC, with Obi emerging as its presidential candidate and Kwankwaso agreeing to work with him. “The opposition has to come together for us to win. The opposition have already come together. Nobody said the coalition must happen on ADC. It can happen in NDC, and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has already dropped his ambition,” he said. Abdulkarim said Atiku and other opposition figures were welcome to join the alliance to broaden its national reach. “What we are asking for is for other people to join us, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, to join all of us, so at least we will have the spread that they think they can add,” he added. The NDC campaign chief also dismissed criticism of the party’s campaign structures, arguing that its organisation should not be compared with the Obidient movement and other support groups backing Obi. “How can you compare a party with a support group? We don’t have any problem. They’re all part of the NDC party. We have more than a thousand support groups like that,” he said. On concerns about electoral fraud, Abdulkarim urged Nigerians who feared their votes might not count to support the NDC, promising that the party had developed measures to protect votes during the 2027 elections. He said the party would campaign peacefully across the country and mobilise voters who had lost confidence in the electoral process. “We are going to do our campaign peacefully. We are going to go into every corner,” he said. Abdulkarim added that the party would reassure voters before the election that their votes would be protected. “I can promise anybody, anybody that feels he wants his vote to count, we have a very, very unique and serious programme that we have put in place,” he said. item.title: Ebonyi Assembly unanimously backs state police bill
item.description: The Ebonyi House of Assembly on Tuesday unanimously approved a bill seeking to establish state police services, endorsing a constitutional amendment transmitted by the National Assembly. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that all 24 members voted in favour of the bill after extensive deliberations and consultations with their constituents. The proposed amendment seeks to alter the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to provide a legal framework for state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force at federal level. The Speaker, Moses Odunwa, said the unanimous decision demonstrated the assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at strengthening the state’s security architecture. “This will also enhance access to criminal intelligence and protection of lives and properties,” Odunwa said. He described the demand for sub-national policing as a longstanding aspiration among Ebonyi residents. “The demand for a sub-national policing system has been an age-long clamour among Ebonyi people,” he said. Odunwa added that the state had formally presented its position in support of state police during a public hearing organised by the National Assembly on constitutional review. He said the bill’s passage reflected residents’ desire for a policing system closer to communities and more responsive to local security challenges. The Leader of the House, Kingsley Ikoro, said establishing state police would significantly increase manpower in the state’s security sector. Ikoro, who represents Afikpo North West under the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the proposed system would improve efforts to tackle crime at grassroots level. Other lawmakers, including Victor Nwoke (APC–Abakaliki North) and Oluchukwu Ezeali (APC–Afikpo North East), also stressed the importance of bringing policing closer to communities. They argued that decentralised policing could help address Nigeria’s security challenges by improving local responses to crime and criminal activities. Following the bill’s passage, Odunwa directed the Clerk of the House, Mrs Uche Edene, to formally transmit the assembly’s resolutions to the National Assembly. item.title: Why 5G remains out of reach for most Nigerians
item.description: …High cost of devices, coverage remains uneven …As smartphone market contracts 11% amid rising device prices …Africa’s budget smartphone shipments plunge 34% amid rising costs By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s mobile market has shifted significantly towards newer network technologies over the past three years, but 5G remains out of reach for most consumers. High smartphone prices, uneven network coverage and rising infrastructure costs continue to limit adoption, despite growing demand for mobile data. In May 2023, 2G accounted for 58.36 percent of reported mobile connections, while 4G represented 25.06 percent and 5G just 0.12 percent. By August 2026, 4G had become the leading technology at 54.77 percent, while 2G fell to 36.05 percent. 5G increased to 4.92 percent. The data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, show progress but underline how slowly the newest technology is reaching the wider population. Chief Technology Officer of NATCOM Development and Investment Limited, trading as NTEL, Kingsley Uwazie, said Nigerians had a strong appetite for data consumption, but the cost of accessing 5G remained a significant barrier. “The 5G ecosystem is in its maturity phase. It has been proven that there is an appetite. Nigerians have an appetite to consume data. But there is a barrier to acquiring the devices and using the technology,” he said. High cost of compatible devices Consumers need 5G-enabled smartphones to access the technology, but rising device prices are making upgrades increasingly difficult, particularly for low-income earners. Uwazie said 5G devices remained expensive despite subsidies offered by some operators. “5G, at the moment, is not a cheap technology to deploy or to own. The cost of 5G devices has been high,” he said. He cited MTN Nigeria and Airtel Nigeria as operators subsidising selected devices, adding that a phone available for about N50, 000 with a subsidy could cost more than N200, 000 without it. The affordability challenge has intensified as Nigeria’s smartphone market contracted by 11 percent in the second quarter of 2026, according to technology research firm Omdia. Rising memory-chip costs, partly linked to growing demand from artificial intelligence, AI, data centres, have increased pressure on manufacturers and consumers. Across Africa, shipments of smartphones priced below $100 fell by 34 percent year-on-year during the quarter. In Nigeria, a market assessment published by technology news platform Condia found that prices of selected Tecno, Infinix, Oppo and itel models increased between January and June 2026. The midpoint price of the itel S-Series Ultra rose from about N263, 500 to N316,400, while the Infinix Zero Series increased from approximately N550,000 to N637,500. Omdia warned in June that Nigerian smartphone prices could rise by another 15 to 30 percent through the remainder of 2026 if component costs continued increasing. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 28, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira maintained relative stability against the United States Dollar across both official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Continued liquidity injections by the Central Bank of Nigeria and sustained foreign currency inflows from autonomous channels have helped cushion the local currency against aggressive market pressures. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, the Naira traded around 1,341.31 to 1,352.87 per Dollar. Spot market activity recorded moderate intra-day fluctuations as commercial banks and institutional buyers satisfied forex demand for import bills and capital remittances. The tight corridor underscores ongoing market clearing measures established under the refined operational framework of the central bank. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, Bureau De Change operators and street currency traders in major hubs such as Lagos, Abuja, and Kano quoted buying rates near 1,375 Naira per Dollar and selling rates around 1,390 Naira per Dollar. This keeps the premium between the official window and the unauthorised market relatively narrow. Financial analysts attribute the steadying market conditions to disciplined monetary policy, steady national foreign exchange reserves hovering around key operational benchmarks, and balanced seasonal demand. Market participants expect trading volumes to remain steady over the near term as both official and informal windows absorb regular commercial order flows. item.title: FG kicks off $100m Southeast gas pipeline project
item.description: …As SEDC seals deal with GasSync, commits $3m .. Tinubu says S’East must rise from potential to reality …Mbah, governors hail Tinubu, pledge support for 400km pipeline The Federal Government, through the South East Development Commission (SEDC) has kicked off a $100 million gas distribution pipeline project to boost industrialisation, attract investments and create jobs in the South East. The 400-kilometre pipeline, designed to connect gas resources to industrial and commercial centres across Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Abia and Ebonyi states, has about 150 potential customers identified, with projected demand of 254 million standard cubic feet of gas per day. The investment agreement for the project was signed on Tuesday at the South-East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony held at Hotel Presidential, Enugu, marking a significant step towards establishing a regional gas distribution network. Tinubu, represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, described the project as a strategic investment that would connect the region’s natural gas resources to industries, strengthen manufacturing and unlock economic opportunities across the five states. “The Southeast’s entrepreneurial spirit is one of Nigeria’s greatest economic assets. I have always believed that the prosperity of the Southeast is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria,” the President said. He said the project aligned with his administration’s commitment to building an integrated regional economy, stressing that gas infrastructure should support industrial development across state boundaries rather than serve isolated markets. “Gas infrastructure must therefore serve industries and markets, not stop at political boundaries. That is the economic logic of regional integration,” he said. The President said the pipeline would benefit manufacturers in Aba, strengthen industrial clusters in Nnewi and Onitsha, attract productive enterprises to Enugu, expand agro-processing and manufacturing in Ebonyi and connect Imo’s gas resources to the wider regional economy. He, however, said the ambition extended beyond supplying existing factories to creating the conditions for new industries, industrial parks and investments that had stalled because of unreliable energy supply. “Our ambition is not simply to deliver gas to existing factories. It is to make possible factories that do not yet exist, industrial parks yet to be developed, and investments that have remained on the drawing board because reliable energy was unavailable,” Tinubu said. He described the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) as an institution established to deliver measurable development outcomes, urging it to assess its performance by the investments it mobilised, infrastructure it enabled, opportunities it created and lives it improved. item.title: PANDEF@10: Leaders push for 50% derivation
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THE Pan Niger Delta Forum, PANDEF, the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone has called for a total overhaul of the region, demand an increase in the derivation allocation to oil-producing states from the current minimum of 13 percent to 50 percent. It also wants accelerated completion of the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway and urgent environmental remediation across the Niger Delta. PANDEF urged the Federal Government, the Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission, RMAFC, and the National Assembly to initiate measures to raise the allocation to at least 50 percent, just as it argued that the minimum 13 percent derivation allocation had remained unchanged for more than two decades, despite the environmental damage and economic difficulties facing oil-producing communities. Addressing newsmen in Abuja, yesterday, after a meeting of the organisation’s Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, virtually to mark the 10 years of existence of the organisation, PANDEF National Chairman, Amb. Godknows Igali, said: “The minimum 13 percent derivation allocation had remained unchanged for more than two decades, despite the environmental damage and economic difficulties facing oil-producing communities. We are demanding an upward review to 50 percent. “We also demand the abolition of the onshore/offshore dichotomy in revenue allocation. We insist that offshore oil and gas operations could damage marine ecosystems and fishing grounds relied upon by coastal communities.” The meeting was attended by the Board of Trustees Chairman and former Akwa Ibom State Governor, Obong Victor Attah, former Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, Kanu Agabi, SAN, PANDEF National Publicity Secretary, Minimising Obiuwevbi, alongside political leaders, traditional rulers and other stakeholders from the six South-South states. Further Igali said: “We propose exploring a market-based South-South investment fund to mobilise resources from individuals, businesses, institutions and other stakeholders for investment in critical sectors. The proposed fund would support enterprise development, improve regional connectivity and create jobs, with the organisation planning to engage private-sector players and other partners to develop a workable framework.” On the 2027 elections, he said: “We called on the people of the South-South to exercise their civic responsibilities peacefully and vote according to their conscience, choosing candidates at all levels whose programmes, commitments, and demonstrate capacity align with the aspirations of the region and who can contribute meaningfully to the peace, progress, and development of the Niger Delta. “Also as the country prepares for the elections, we are calling for a framework that extend to environmental remediation to other polluted communities. item.title: Last moments of Katsina cleric, Masussuka
item.description: Family and neighbours of the slain Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, have recalled the chain of events preceding his gruesome murder in front of his residence in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, on Monday evening. Masussuka was shot dead alongside his associate, Adamu Abubakar, in an attack claimed by the extremist group Ansaru. The killing has plunged his family, followers and associates into mourning. This is as Amnesty International called on the government to conduct a thorough investigation into the killing and ensure that those responsible were brought to justice. Hours before the incident, at a gathering in his father-in-law’s residence where relatives and well-wishers had assembled to mourn a deceased family member, the cleric had reportedly spoken about the inevitability of death and the need for people to live harmoniously. ‘How my 5 children died in tricycle-tanker crash’ Bangkok’s debt debate: Can Africa secure fairer development finance? Masussuka was said to have reminded the mourners that differences in race, tribe, nationality and social standing should not divide humanity because everyone would eventually return to Allah. A resident, Murtala Narega, who was familiar with the cleric’s final hours, said Masussuka used the gathering at his father-in-law’s residence to remind mourners that differences among people should encourage understanding rather than hostility. “He reminded us that Allah created people differently, but those differences should not be a reason for division or hostility,” Narega said. According to him, the cleric also spoke about the certainty of death, regardless of a person’s wealth, position, or circumstances. “He told us that this world is only a temporary place and that everyone will eventually return to Allah. He advised us to use the time we have to do good and serve humanity,” he said. Narega said the message had become particularly painful following the cleric’s death just hours later. “None of us imagined that we would be mourning him so soon after listening to him speak about death. His words have stayed with us because he reminded us that life is temporary, but we did not know that his own end was so close,” he added. After the gathering, Masussuka reportedly returned to the studio at his residence, where he regularly delivered religious lectures to his followers online. The wife of the late cleric, Hajiya Fatima, recalled that Masussuka had reminded her of the oneness of Allah before he stepped out on the fateful day, adding that shortly afterwards, she heard gunshots. “My husband spoke to me about the oneness of Allah before he left home. Shortly after he left, I heard about four gunshots. item.title: 4 students, one lady killed in Niger governor’s convoy road crash
item.description: By Clare Nnabuike, Minna Five person, four male students and a young lady have died in a fatal accident involving the Niger state governor Mohammed Umaru Bago’s convoy in Minna, the state capital. The incident happened on Monday at Gidan Mangoro community along the Minna–Bida Road. It followed a head-on collision between a high speeding Hilux van in the convoy of Bago, and a private Peugeot 206 car. The lady identified as Mrs Nafisa was driving the car and died at the spot of the accident. She was said to be a staff of an NGO, and Programme Manager at Labspace, and the Founder of Wosh Mart Service Ltd. A resident of Gidan Mangoro, Abdullahi Musa, told Vanguard that the accident occurred at about 11:35am when the governor was returning from Bida. He and his team paid a condolence visit on the Etsu Nupe and chairman of the Niger state council of traditional rulers Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar over the passage of the Sagi Nupe Hajia Aisha. He said the occupants of the private car driven by Nafisa were suspected to be postgraduate students of the Federal University of Technology, Minna. His words, “The people in the private car died instantly, while those in the government Hilux sustained serious injuries with the driver dying on the spot. Nafisa “The accident was caused by wrongful overtaking by the Hilux in the governor’s convoy. The other car was in its lane when the Hilux rammed into it.” A member of staff of Minna General Hospital, where the victims were rushed to told Vanguard that three people died on the spot while two other people died due to high level of injuries sustain from the crash. “Some of the injured victims were subsequently referred to IBB Specialist Hospital for advanced medical care,” he said. Vanguard gathered that one of the occupants of the Hilux van was a former Niger state local government council chairman who sustained fractures to his legs but was still alive at the time of this report. The Niger State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC Aishat Sa’adu, confirmed the road crash but said that by the time her officers arrived at the scene, the victims had already been evacuated to the hospital. The Police Public Relations Officer of the Niger state command Superintendent of Police Wasiu Abiodun confirmed the incident and said the accident was under investigation. He did not however give the names or numbers of the deceased. “The accident occured this morning and we are investigating it,” Abiodun said. item.title: State Police: Presidency seeks private sector support for funding, blueprint
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA—THE Presidency has challenged Nigeria’s organised private sector to develop a comprehensive financing and implementation blueprint for the proposed state police system, saying that businesses must take an active role in building the security institutions required to protect investments, create jobs and strengthen economic resilience. Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Mr. Femi Gbajabiamila, who made the challenge, tasked the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, chambers of commerce and business associations with producing practical proposals for financing, institutional management and accountable partnerships to support the decentralisation of policing. Speaking during a plenary session on “Security, Stability and Economic Resilience” at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, in Abuja, on Monday, Gbajabiamila said President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to establishing state police presented an opportunity for businesses to contribute directly to the development of security institutions capable of supporting sustainable economic growth. According to him: “I, therefore, ask the Nigerian Economic Summit Group to carry this engagement beyond our meeting. Bring forward a considered private sector contribution on financing and implementing state police, with practical proposals for accountable partnerships. ”Take that work into the legislative process and into your engagement with state governments. For our part, we remain answerable for turning reform into protection that people can rely on,” he said. Gbajabiamila urged business leaders to engage governors and legislators on the proposed reform, drawing attention to the relationship between effective local policing, employment generation and investment decisions. ”Your participation should also improve the substance of the reform. As the legislative process proceeds, examine the proposals for financing and oversight. Bring your experience of managing institutions and controlling expenditure to that discussion. Help us understand the security failures that prevent viable projects from proceeding,” he stated. item.title: Agric ministry puts post-harvest loss at $10bn yearly
item.description: •As 14 of 17 federal silos fail •20% of grains, 70% of fruits, vegetables lost By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — THE Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, Tuesday, disclosed that Nigeria loses an estimated $10 billion annually to post-harvest losses. Kyari made this known as one of the panelists focusing on the topic ‘Productivity Revolution for Growth’ at the ongoing 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#32) organised by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, in Abuja. He also said Nigeria loses between 15 and 20 per cent of its grains, including rice, maize and millet, while losses involving tomatoes, pepper, onions, fruits and vegetables could reach 60 to 70 per cent, depending on the season. He described the reduction of post-harvest losses as a low-hanging fruit in Nigeria’s food security drive, said the country could significantly improve food availability and farmers’ earnings by addressing weaknesses in storage, processing, transportation and market infrastructure. He stated: “We lose almost about $10 billion annually on post-harvest losses. “About 15 to 20 per cent on grains, and you can see grains that are hard, and you probably think we will not lose much of that, but we lose on grains, on cereal, rice, maize, and so on and so forth, millet. On fruits and vegetables, the minister warned that the scale of waste was considerably higher. “Tomato, pepper, onion, and other fruits and vegetables, we lose some of that as high as 60 to 70 per cent depending on the season”, Kyari said, attributing the vulnerability of tomatoes, in particular, to their short shelf life and the effects of hot weather. The Minister also lamented that 17 of the 33 silo complexes built by the Federal Government had been concessioned to private operators, but only three were performing. “The government had concessioned 17 out of the 33 silos that it had built over a period of time, but I’ll tell you that out of the 17, only three have performed. All the 14 are almost comatose for the past, I believe, since when it was concessioned”, he said. The minister attributed the problem partly to a disconnect between agricultural production centres and the location of storage facilities. According to him, some farming communities are situated more than 100 kilometres from major storage facilities, making it difficult and costly for farmers to transport their produce to the silos. He argued that the country’s storage strategy must be redesigned to reflect the geographical distribution of agricultural production rather than depend exclusively on large-scale facilities located far from farming communities. The minister’s position suggests that the challenge extends beyond the physical availability of silos to questions of accessibility, operational efficiency, commercial viability and the suitability of infrastructure to the needs of farmers. item.title: Miners’ deaths: Panel recommends summary dismissal, prosecution of NSCDC officers, N1.4bn for victims
item.description: •Says overcrowding, heat stress, dehydration caused deaths •Rules out use of chemicals; as FG vows justice By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—An independent ministerial committee has recommended summary dismissal, administrative sanctions and prosecution of some officers of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, over the deaths of 33 detainees in the custody of its Niger State command in Minna, along with N1.4 billion in compensation for victims and survivors. The committee’s chairman, Jonathan Kure, who presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja, yesterday, described the deaths as “entirely preventable.” Kure said the committee concluded that the incident was a preventable custodial tragedy, caused by severe overcrowding, unlawful and unsuitable detention conditions, failure of duty of care, disregard of repeated distress warnings, inadequate supervision, and wider systemic deficiencies. He said the evidence did not support claims that the deaths resulted from a disease outbreak. According to him, “available medical and forensic evidence instead indicated that the fatalities resulted from an environmental asphyxia, an acute respiratory failure caused by prolonged confinement in a severely overcrowded and poorly ventilated detention cell, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.” The 65-page report, of which 46 pages form the main body, examined the arrest, detention, treatment and deaths of detainees between September 15 and 17, 2026. It was commissioned by the minister, following a presidential directive. The committee said the tragedy stemmed from enforcement operations against suspected illegal mining in and around Minna. No headquarter’s approval Kure said: “The operation was undertaken without an approved operational order, proper planning and consultation with relevant mining authorities, or involvement of the specialised Mining Marshals unit. National headquarters was not informed before the operation commenced,” he added. He said the raids led to the arrest of men, women and children, and that by the evening of September 16, 75 persons had been detained. He said after one release, 74 remained in custody overnight, with about 50 male detainees confined in a cell measuring about 20 square metres. The committee said the cell had “a solid metal door, inadequate airflow, no running water, poor lighting, and no functioning toilet.” It said food and drinking water were either unavailable or grossly inadequate, adding that adults and minors were held together. It found that the conditions breached constitutional safeguards, the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, the Child Rights Act and accepted international standards. item.title: Atiku to Tinubu: $20.5bn loan plan vindicates my warning
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has said President Bola Tinubu’s request for approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion vindicates his earlier warning about a proposed $20 billion loan, accusing the administration of failing to disclose the specific projects the funds would finance. Atiku said the absence of project-by-project details raises questions about transparency and the possibility of public funds being channelled to political allies and favoured contractors, particularly through the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway project, which he alleged had been rerouted inland. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku recalled that he had warned on October 12 about the reported borrowing plan and challenged Tinubu to confirm or deny it and publish the relevant accounts. “Today, he has asked the Senate to approve $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external loans. My warning has been vindicated,” he said. Atiku faulted the President for failing to provide details of the projects, their costs, locations and contractors, insisting that Nigerians should not be asked to shoulder such a huge debt without knowing how the money would be spent. He questioned whether the highway project could become a conduit for directing borrowed funds to political allies, especially with an election approaching. “Is this a development plan for Nigerians or a campaign financing scheme dressed up as infrastructure?” he asked. The ADC candidate warned that he would scrutinise loans obtained during the final year of Tinubu’s administration if elected President, vowing to challenge any borrowing found to have breached constitutional, statutory or due process requirements. “I put local and international lenders on notice: any loan granted to this winding-down administration must meet all constitutional, statutory and due process requirements,” he said. He urged the National Assembly to withhold approval until the President publishes the projects, contracts, costs, contractors, loan terms and repayment obligations attached to the borrowing plan. “No public money should be borrowed in the dark, and no lawmaker should sign a blank cheque against Nigeria’s future,” Atiku said. He said the burden of proof rested on Tinubu to demonstrate that the loans would serve the national interest rather than political interests, warning that Nigerians struggling with the cost of living should not be made to pay for debts incurred without adequate public disclosure. Atiku said the controversy could further shape the political contest, with voters having an opportunity to hold the administration accountable for its borrowing decisions. item.title: FG Approves Six-Month ₦70,000 Transport Support For Workers
item.description: The Federal Government has approved a ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a conciliation meeting with the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). The agreement was reached at a meeting convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on Tuesday, October 27, to address issues raised by organised labour. Under the agreement, the government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, with payments scheduled to begin in November in three equal monthly instalments. The parties, however, failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage, although they agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and begin meeting immediately. The resolutions were contained in a press statement issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment after the meeting, which was chaired by the Minister, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, with NLC President Joe Ajaero leading the labour delegation. On the transport intervention, the statement said the Federal Government “will pay a transport intervention of Seventy Thousand Naira (₦70,000) across all levels for a period of six (6) months, commencing from November 2026.” On peculiar allowances, the government approved payments with effect from May 1, 2026, with the arrears to be paid in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The statement also addressed outstanding allowances for health workers, stating that “Nineteen (19) months arrears of allowances for health workers will be redeemed within three (3) months with effect from December 2026.” On hazard allowances for agricultural workers, the ministry said the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security had submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. The parties also discussed the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) adjustment. According to the statement, NSIWC promised to complete the update of the cost implications within three weeks to enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to decide on the adjustment. On tax relief for workers, the statement said the issue would be taken to the National Executive Council because taxation is a statutory matter. The meeting followed an earlier conciliation session held on October 22 and came after discussions on issues raised by the NLC’s Central Working Committee and National Executive Council. item.title: First Israeli Election Exit Polls Show Narrow Edge For Opposition
item.description: The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday, but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The country’s main pollsters — Channels 11, 12 and 13 — projected the opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats. Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them. In the last election, Likud had walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Netanyahu’s traditional allies balked at the corruption cases the premier was facing. This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party — projected to nab 21 to 23 seats — to form an opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu. A volunteer stands behind a banner for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party at a polling station in Jerusalem on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel’s legislative election. Photo by Jewel SAMAD / AFP) “The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Eisenkot said. Israel’s current opposition chief Yair Lapid said Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”. While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it. Tuesday’s poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future. item.title: ‘What Are You Doing With The Money?’ Umeh Questions Tinubu’s Fresh Loan Request
item.description: The Senator representing Anambra Central, Victor Umeh, has questioned how the Federal Government has spent funds from previous borrowings, asking why budgetary obligations remain unmet despite repeated approvals for loans. Umeh spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday while reacting to President Bola Tinubu’s request to the National Assembly for approval to borrow an additional $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion. The senator argued that previous borrowing requests were justified on the grounds that the funds would finance government budgets, yet contractors were still owed for capital projects. “The truth is that we have approved so much funds to be borrowed in the past, and on each occasion we’ve been told that this borrowing would be able to fund the budgets and these budgets have remained unfunded up till this day,” Umeh said. ﻿ He noted that three budgets were running concurrently, while the government had yet to meet its obligations to contractors handling capital projects. “Three budgets are running concurrently and the government is not meeting its obligations to contractors on capital projects and so on and so forth. So if you borrow to finance a budget and you are not able to finance that budget, where has the money gone to? That is the question in the lips of everybody,” he said. Umeh also suggested that the latest loan request would eventually receive legislative approval, arguing that opposition lawmakers would be outvoted by members of the ruling party. President Tinubu has written to the National Assembly seeking approval for the Federal Government’s 2026–2027 supplementary external borrowing plan, valued at $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion. The government says the proposed loans would fund critical infrastructure, agriculture, education and other key sectors of the economy in line with the administration’s development priorities. The request has added to the debate over the government’s borrowing plans and Nigeria’s rising debt burden. item.title: Tinubu’s Difficult Reforms Beginning To Bear Fruit, Says Adesina
item.description: Former African Development Bank (AfDB) President Akinwunmi Adesina has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms are beginning to yield results, citing increased foreign exchange availability, renewed portfolio investments and a downward trend in inflation. Adesina, who visited Tinubu on Tuesday, described the removal of the petrol subsidy and the harmonisation of exchange rate windows as “very important, difficult reforms”, adding that the government must now focus on translating economic stabilisation into growth and prosperity. Speaking to State House correspondents after the meeting, the former AfDB chief said Nigeria’s international perception had also improved, pointing to the outlooks assigned to the country by rating agencies. “If you look at it, you have a lot more FX available today. You have a lot of portfolio investors that are coming into the country. You have inflation trending downwards. Prices are still a bit high, but inflation is trending downwards,” he said. ﻿ Adesina added that some rating agencies had given Nigeria stable or positive outlooks, describing the development as an indication of changing perceptions of the country. He, however, said the gains from the reforms should be followed by a stronger focus on structural transformation and economic expansion. “Now that’s just the beginning of the work. I think the most critical thing is the president realised this, and everybody knows that being a dentist is not a very difficult job. But you have to also now move from the issue of the reforms and stabilisation, straight into structural transformation and also growth and prosperity, which is what the president is focusing on,” he said. Adesina also expressed his willingness to contribute to Nigeria’s development in any capacity the President considers appropriate, insisting that he was not seeking a political appointment. “I told the President, I’m back at home, here to help and ready to help. It’s my country. I love my country, and I’m ready to help,” he said. Asked in what capacity he could support Nigeria, given his experience on the international stage, Adesina said he was prepared to serve wherever his contribution would be useful. “I’m fully able to help Nigeria in any capacity. I’ve always had that. You know, my heart is always at home. And in any capacity that His Excellency feels I can help, I can help in anything. I’m not looking for a job. I’m not looking for anything. I’m just here to help,” he said. “It’s my country. I have a duty, an obligation, and a responsibility to do so, and I will.” Adesina also briefed Tinubu on his 10-year tenure as AfDB president, which ended after two terms, and the bank’s support for Nigeria during that period. He said the AfDB provided about $7 billion in financing to Nigeria between 2015 and 2025, compared with $11.1 billion in total financing since the bank began operations in the country in 1971. “So, within 10 years, we were able to do 63 percent, literally, of that,” he said
